prompt recall — recall_prev, recall_next

L263–L322

↑/↓ on an empty prompt. The state is history_index: Option<usize> — None means "editing a fresh line", Some(i) means "browsing entry i".

edited_since_recall is the good detail: if the buffer no longer matches what was loaded, you have edited it, so navigation ends rather than clobbering your half-typed message. That is why the README says clear the line and press ↑ to browse again.

Stepping past the newest entry returns to an empty line rather than sticking, which matches how shells behave.

prompt_history is deliberately separate from history: it is your typed prompts, not the model conversation, and it survives /clear.

263 
264 /// Recall the previous prompt (`Up`).
265 ///
266 /// From a fresh, empty line this loads the most recent prompt; while already
267 /// browsing it steps further back in time. Editing a recalled entry ends
268 /// navigation, so a stray `Up` never clobbers a half-typed message.
269 pub fn recall_prev(&mut self) {
270 match self.history_index {
271 None => {
272 if !self.input.is_blank() || self.prompt_history.is_empty() {
273 return;
274 }
275 let i = self.prompt_history.len() - 1;
276 self.load_history_entry(i);
277 }
278 Some(i) => {
279 if self.edited_since_recall(i) {
280 self.history_index = None;
281 return;
282 }
283 if i > 0 {
284 self.load_history_entry(i - 1);
285 }
286 // Already at the oldest entry: stay put.
287 }
288 }
289 }
290 
291 /// Recall the next (more recent) prompt (`Down`).
292 ///
293 /// Only does anything while browsing. Stepping past the newest entry returns
294 /// to an empty prompt.
295 pub fn recall_next(&mut self) {
296 let Some(i) = self.history_index else {
297 return;
298 };
299 if self.edited_since_recall(i) {
300 self.history_index = None;
301 return;
302 }
303 if i + 1 < self.prompt_history.len() {
304 self.load_history_entry(i + 1);
305 } else {
306 // Past the newest: back to a fresh, empty line.
307 self.history_index = None;
308 self.input.clear();
309 }
310 }
311 
312 /// True if the buffer no longer matches the entry we loaded — i.e. the user
313 /// edited it, so navigation should end.
314 fn edited_since_recall(&self, i: usize) -> bool {
315 self.prompt_history.get(i).map(String::as_str) != Some(self.input.text())
316 }
317 
318 fn load_history_entry(&mut self, i: usize) {
319 self.history_index = Some(i);
320 self.input.clear();
321 self.input.insert_str(&self.prompt_history[i].clone());
322 }

generations, request timing, cost accessors

L323–L357

next_generation is called in two places — when spawning a task, and in cancel. That second call is the whole mechanism: bumping the counter without spawning anything invalidates every update the abandoned task had already queued.

mark_request_done is called on every ending — success, error, and cancel — because that time was really spent waiting on the model.

323 
324 /// Bump the generation and return the new value. Every spawned task is
325 /// tagged with the generation current when it started, so a later cancel can
326 /// invalidate its still-queued updates.
327 pub fn next_generation(&mut self) -> u64 {
328 self.generation += 1;
329 self.generation
330 }
331 
332 /// The generation identifying the current in-flight task.
333 pub fn generation(&self) -> u64 {
334 self.generation
335 }
336 
337 /// Note that a request has just gone out, starting the clock on it.
338 pub fn mark_request_sent(&mut self) {
339 self.request_started = Some(std::time::Instant::now());
340 }
341 
342 /// Note that the in-flight request has ended, however it ended. Failed and
343 /// cancelled requests are still counted: that time was really spent.
344 pub fn mark_request_done(&mut self) {
345 if let Some(started) = self.request_started.take() {
346 self.ledger.add_wait(started.elapsed());
347 }
348 }
349 
350 /// The `/cost` breakdown, and the compact status-bar form beside it.
351 pub fn cost_report(&self) -> String {
352 self.ledger.report(self.price_in, self.price_out)
353 }
354 
355 pub fn cost_status(&self) -> String {
356 self.ledger.status_line(self.price_in, self.price_out)
357 }

cancel, push_delta, finish_stream

L358–L391

cancel is the Esc path. Four steps: record the wait time, bump the generation, drop the live stream view, return to Idle. Note the doc comment's division of labour — this invalidates the updates; main.rs signals the task to stop its actual work.

push_delta/finish_stream manage the display-only streaming buffer. finish_stream simply throws the accumulated text away, because the authoritative text arrives with the completion and is committed through push_response instead.

cancel clears pending_fetch. A parked fetch has not been spawned yet, so dropping it is the whole job — a fetch already in flight is stopped by its cancel signal instead, and its result is discarded as stale.

358 
359 /// Interrupt the in-flight turn: invalidate its updates, drop the live
360 /// stream view, and return control to the user. The caller is responsible
361 /// for signalling the task to stop its actual work.
362 pub fn cancel(&mut self) {
363 if !self.is_busy() {
364 return;
365 }
366 // A parked fetch has not been spawned yet, so dropping it here is all
367 // that is needed; a spawned one is stopped by its cancel signal.
368 self.pending_fetch = None;
369 self.mark_request_done();
370 // A fresh generation means any update still queued from the abandoned
371 // task will be recognised as stale and dropped.
372 self.next_generation();
373 self.finish_stream();
374 self.status = Status::Idle;
375 self.push_notice("Cancelled.");
376 }
377 
378 /// Append a streamed token chunk to the live reply view.
379 pub fn push_delta(&mut self, delta: &str) {
380 self.status = Status::Streaming;
381 self.streaming
382 .get_or_insert_with(String::new)
383 .push_str(delta);
384 self.follow = true;
385 }
386 
387 /// Discard the live streaming view. The full reply text is committed
388 /// separately via [`App::push_response`].
389 pub fn finish_stream(&mut self) {
390 self.streaming = None;
391 }

the completion menu

L392–L440

completions() is derived from the input buffer on every call, never cached. The doc comment says why: a cache can drift out of step with what has been typed, and this cannot.

completion_index() clamps on read rather than on write — also deliberate, since the list shrinks as you type and a stored cursor would otherwise end up pointing past the end.

move_completion uses rem_euclid so the highlight wraps at both ends (unlike the session picker, which clamps).

392 
393 /// Commands offered for the partially-typed name in the prompt.
394 ///
395 /// Derived from the input buffer rather than cached, so it can never drift
396 /// out of step with what has been typed.
397 pub fn completions(&self) -> Vec<&'static command::Spec> {
398 if self.is_busy() {
399 return Vec::new();
400 }
401 match command::completion_prefix(self.input.text()) {
402 Some(prefix) => command::matching(prefix),
403 None => Vec::new(),
404 }
405 }
406 
407 /// Index of the highlighted completion, clamped to what is actually offered.
408 /// Clamping here means the stored cursor can never point past the list after
409 /// the prefix narrows it.
410 pub fn completion_index(&self) -> usize {
411 let count = self.completions().len();
412 if count == 0 {
413 0
414 } else {
415 self.completion_cursor.min(count - 1)
416 }
417 }
418 
419 /// Move the highlight, wrapping in both directions.
420 pub fn move_completion(&mut self, delta: isize) {
421 let count = self.completions().len();
422 if count == 0 {
423 return;
424 }
425 let current = self.completion_index() as isize;
426 let next = (current + delta).rem_euclid(count as isize);
427 self.completion_cursor = next as usize;
428 }
429 
430 /// Replace the typed name with the highlighted command. Returns false when
431 /// there was nothing to complete.
432 pub fn accept_completion(&mut self) -> bool {
433 let Some(spec) = self.completions().get(self.completion_index()).copied() else {
434 return false;
435 };
436 self.input.clear();
437 self.input.insert_str(&format!("/{}", spec.name));
438 self.completion_cursor = 0;
439 true
440 }

frame() and run_command()

L441–L472

run_command is the local command dispatcher — nothing here reaches the model, which is the guarantee command.rs exists to provide.

Most arms delegate to a method below. Unknown posts a notice naming the typo and pointing at /help.

self.follow = true at the end applies to every command, so running one always scrolls you back to the bottom to see its output.

441 
442 /// Record a raw protocol payload. Kept regardless of debug mode so turning
443 /// `/debug` on later still shows what already happened.
444 fn frame(&mut self, direction: Direction, body: impl Into<String>) {
445 self.transcript.push(Entry::Frame {
446 direction,
447 body: body.into(),
448 });
449 }
450 
451 /// Handle a locally-executed slash command. Nothing here reaches the model.
452 pub fn run_command(&mut self, command: Command) {
453 match command {
454 Command::Debug => {
455 self.debug = !self.debug;
456 let state = if self.debug { "on" } else { "off" };
457 self.push_notice(format!("Debug mode {state}."));
458 }
459 Command::Help => self.push_notice(crate::command::help_text()),
460 Command::Clear => self.reset_conversation(),
461 Command::Quit => self.should_quit = true,
462 Command::Save(name) => self.save_session(name),
463 Command::Load(name) => self.load_session_command(name),
464 Command::Rename(name) => self.rename_session(name),
465 Command::Fork(name) => self.fork_session(name),
466 Command::Cost => self.push_notice(self.cost_report()),
467 Command::Unknown(name) => self.push_notice(format!(
468 "Unknown command /{name}. Type /help to see what is available."
469 )),
470 }
471 self.follow = true;
472 }

to_session, apply_session, fingerprint

L473–L511

Both halves of persistence, and both are pure — no I/O. That is why they can be tested directly and why the I/O lives in session.rs.

apply_session resets the view state along with the data (scroll, follow, history_index), so a loaded session opens at the bottom in a clean state.

The model-mismatch notice is pushed after the transcript is replaced — the comment says so, and getting it backwards would have the replacement wipe the notice.

473 
474 /// Snapshot the current session for persistence. Pure.
475 pub fn to_session(&self) -> crate::session::Session {
476 crate::session::Session::new(
477 self.model.clone(),
478 self.history.clone(),
479 self.transcript.clone(),
480 self.prompt_history.clone(),
481 self.ledger.clone(),
482 )
483 }
484 
485 /// Replace the in-memory session with a loaded one. Pure — does no I/O.
486 pub fn apply_session(&mut self, session: crate::session::Session) {
487 let model_mismatch = (session.model != self.model).then(|| session.model.clone());
488 
489 self.history = session.history;
490 self.transcript = session.transcript;
491 self.prompt_history = session.prompt_history;
492 self.ledger = session.ledger;
493 self.finish_stream();
494 self.status = Status::Idle;
495 self.scroll = 0;
496 self.follow = true;
497 self.history_index = None;
498 
499 // Pushed after the transcript is replaced, or it would be overwritten.
500 if let Some(saved_model) = model_mismatch {
501 self.push_notice(format!(
502 "Loaded a session saved with model {saved_model}; new turns use {}.",
503 self.model
504 ));
505 }
506 }
507 
508 /// A cheap fingerprint of the persisted state, to skip redundant writes.
509 fn fingerprint(&self) -> (usize, usize) {
510 (self.history.len(), self.transcript.len())
511 }

persist_current and maybe_autosave

L512–L544

Auto-save is always on. maybe_autosave is called after every event-loop iteration, and its three guards are what make that cheap and correct:

  • Must be Idle — never write mid-turn.
  • history.len() > 1 — past the bare system prompt, so a session that never started does not create a file.
  • Fingerprint changed — otherwise it is a no-op.

autosave_failed makes a write failure report once rather than on every turn — a full disk would otherwise fill the transcript with the same error.

512 
513 /// Write the current conversation to `current_session`. Records the
514 /// fingerprint so auto-save won't immediately repeat, and reports a write
515 /// failure at most once per failure streak.
516 fn persist_current(&mut self) {
517 let session = self.to_session();
518 match crate::session::save(&self.sessions_dir, &self.current_session, &session) {
519 Ok(_) => {
520 self.last_saved = self.fingerprint();
521 self.autosave_failed = false;
522 }
523 Err(e) => {
524 if !self.autosave_failed {
525 self.autosave_failed = true;
526 self.transcript
527 .push(Entry::Error(format!("auto-save failed: {e:#}")));
528 }
529 }
530 }
531 }
532 
533 /// Save after a completed turn. A no-op unless idle, past the empty startup
534 /// state, and actually changed — so it neither writes mid-turn nor litters
535 /// the directory before a conversation has begun.
536 pub fn maybe_autosave(&mut self) {
537 if self.status != Status::Idle
538 || self.history.len() <= 1
539 || self.fingerprint() == self.last_saved
540 {
541 return;
542 }
543 self.persist_current();
544 }

save, load, and the picker opener

L545–L596

/save with a name adopts it going forward, so auto-save follows. /load with no name opens the picker; with a name it goes straight to load_named.

load_named is shared by both paths so they cannot behave differently. A failed load leaves the current session completely intact — the error goes to the transcript and nothing is replaced.

Note that these push Entry::Error directly rather than calling push_error: this is a local command failing, not a model turn, so there is no trailing user message to roll back.

545 
546 fn save_session(&mut self, name: Option<String>) {
547 if let Some(name) = name {
548 self.current_session = name;
549 }
550 let session = self.to_session();
551 match crate::session::save(&self.sessions_dir, &self.current_session, &session) {
552 Ok(path) => {
553 self.last_saved = self.fingerprint();
554 self.push_notice(format!("Saved session to {}", path.display()));
555 }
556 // A local command error, not a failed model turn — no history rollback.
557 Err(e) => self.transcript.push(Entry::Error(format!("{e:#}"))),
558 }
559 }
560 
561 fn load_session_command(&mut self, name: Option<String>) {
562 // No name: open the picker (or notice, if there is nothing to pick).
563 let Some(name) = name else {
564 self.open_load_picker();
565 return;
566 };
567 self.load_named(name);
568 }
569 
570 /// Load a session by name, replacing the conversation. Shared by `/load
571 /// <name>` and the picker. A failed load leaves the current session intact.
572 fn load_named(&mut self, name: String) {
573 match crate::session::load(&self.sessions_dir, &name) {
574 Ok(session) => {
575 self.apply_session(session);
576 // Auto-save now continues to the loaded session's file.
577 self.current_session = name.clone();
578 self.last_saved = self.fingerprint();
579 self.push_notice(format!("Loaded session {name:?}."));
580 }
581 Err(e) => self.transcript.push(Entry::Error(format!("{e:#}"))),
582 }
583 }
584 
585 /// Open the session picker, or post a notice when nothing is saved yet.
586 pub fn open_load_picker(&mut self) {
587 let sessions = crate::session::list(&self.sessions_dir);
588 if sessions.is_empty() {
589 self.push_notice("No saved sessions. Use /save [name] to create one.");
590 } else {
591 self.picker = Some(Picker {
592 sessions,
593 selected: 0,
594 });
595 }
596 }

the picker

L597–L635

picker_move clamps; the completion menu wraps. The difference is intentional — a short command list is pleasant to cycle, a long session list is not.

picker_select returns whether i was a real row, which is what makes a click on empty space below the list do nothing at all rather than selecting the last row.

597 
598 pub fn picker(&self) -> Option<&Picker> {
599 self.picker.as_ref()
600 }
601 
602 /// Move the highlight, clamped to the list (no wrap).
603 pub fn picker_move(&mut self, delta: isize) {
604 if let Some(picker) = &mut self.picker {
605 let last = picker.sessions.len().saturating_sub(1);
606 let next = (picker.selected as isize + delta).clamp(0, last as isize);
607 picker.selected = next as usize;
608 }
609 }
610 
611 /// Focus a row directly, for mouse hover/click. Returns whether `i` was a
612 /// real row, so a click on empty space below the list does nothing.
613 pub fn picker_select(&mut self, i: usize) -> bool {
614 if let Some(picker) = &mut self.picker
615 && i < picker.sessions.len()
616 {
617 picker.selected = i;
618 return true;
619 }
620 false
621 }
622 
623 /// Load the highlighted session and close the picker.
624 pub fn picker_confirm(&mut self) {
625 let Some(picker) = self.picker.take() else {
626 return;
627 };
628 if let Some(name) = picker.sessions.into_iter().nth(picker.selected) {
629 self.load_named(name);
630 }
631 }
632 
633 pub fn picker_cancel(&mut self) {
634 self.picker = None;
635 }

rename and fork

L636–L672

/fork is the interesting one. It freezes the original where it is and continues under a new name: persist to the old name, switch, persist to the new one. Both files start identical and diverge from the fork point.

The in-memory conversation is untouched — you keep talking, you just write somewhere else now. That is what makes fork the thing to do before /clear if you want to keep a conversation.

It refuses to fork onto an existing name, so a fork can never destroy a saved session.

636 
637 fn rename_session(&mut self, name: Option<String>) {
638 let Some(new) = name else {
639 self.transcript
640 .push(Entry::Error("usage: /rename <name>".into()));
641 return;
642 };
643 match crate::session::rename(&self.sessions_dir, &self.current_session, &new) {
644 Ok(_) => {
645 self.current_session = new.clone();
646 self.last_saved = self.fingerprint();
647 self.push_notice(format!(
648 "Renamed session to {new:?} (load with /load {new})."
649 ));
650 }
651 Err(e) => self.transcript.push(Entry::Error(format!("{e:#}"))),
652 }
653 }
654 
655 fn fork_session(&mut self, name: Option<String>) {
656 let new = name.unwrap_or_else(crate::session::default_name);
657 if new == self.current_session || crate::session::exists(&self.sessions_dir, &new) {
658 self.transcript.push(Entry::Error(format!(
659 "cannot fork to {new:?}: a session with that name already exists"
660 )));
661 return;
662 }
663 // Freeze the original at its current state, then continue under the new
664 // name. The in-memory conversation is untouched — you keep talking.
665 let original = self.current_session.clone();
666 self.persist_current();
667 self.current_session = new.clone();
668 self.persist_current();
669 self.push_notice(format!(
670 "Forked to session {new:?}; original preserved as {original:?}."
671 ));
672 }

is_busy, pending, is_waiting

L673–L692

is_busy() is the single gate for prompt editing: !matches!(self.status, Status::Idle). Everything else — modal open, command running, tokens streaming — counts as busy.

pending() is how main and ui ask whether the modal is up.

673 
674 /// Waiting specifically on the model. Prefer [`App::is_busy`] for gating
675 /// input; this is the narrower check used by tests.
676 #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]
677 pub fn is_waiting(&self) -> bool {
678 self.status == Status::Waiting
679 }
680 
681 /// True while the harness is busy and the prompt should be inert.
682 pub fn is_busy(&self) -> bool {
683 !matches!(self.status, Status::Idle)
684 }
685 
686 pub fn pending(&self) -> Option<&Pending> {
687 match &self.status {
688 Status::AwaitingApproval(pending) => Some(pending),
689 _ => None,
690 }
691 }
692 

submit and send_prompt — the loop's entry point

L693–L734

submit consumes the buffer and routes it: a slash command runs locally and returns None, so nothing typed as a command ever reaches the model. Otherwise it becomes a prompt.

send_prompt is where a turn begins. Watch the two records diverge in three consecutive lines: the transcript gets what you typed (line 705), while history gets it wrapped in <ai-harness-query> (line 708).

Then the counters reset — iterations, retries, retry_anchor — because a new prompt is a fresh budget, and status becomes Waiting.

Returning Some(self.history.clone()) is the signal to main.rs to spawn a request. The whole conversation is sent every time; the API is stateless.

693 /// Consume the prompt buffer.
694 ///
695 /// A slash command is executed locally and never reaches the model, so this
696 /// returns `None` for those. Otherwise it returns the messages to send.
697 pub fn submit(&mut self) -> Option<Vec<Message>> {
698 if self.is_busy() || self.input.is_blank() {
699 return None;
700 }
701 match crate::command::parse(&self.input.take()) {
702 crate::command::Input::Command(command) => {
703 self.run_command(command);
704 None
705 }
706 crate::command::Input::Prompt(text) => self.send_prompt(text),
707 }
708 }
709 
710 /// Send `text` as a user query, bypassing slash-command parsing.
711 pub fn send_prompt(&mut self, text: String) -> Option<Vec<Message>> {
712 if self.is_busy() || text.trim().is_empty() {
713 return None;
714 }
715 // Record for Up/Down recall, de-duping an immediate repeat. Browsing
716 // ends on submit.
717 if self.prompt_history.last() != Some(&text) {
718 self.prompt_history.push(text.clone());
719 }
720 self.history_index = None;
721 
722 // The transcript shows what the user typed; the model gets it wrapped.
723 self.transcript.push(Entry::User(text.clone()));
724 let encoded = protocol::encode_query(&text);
725 self.frame(Direction::Sent, encoded.clone());
726 self.history.push(Message::user(encoded));
727 
728 self.iterations = 0;
729 self.retries = 0;
730 self.retry_anchor = None;
731 self.status = Status::Waiting;
732 self.follow = true;
733 Some(self.history.clone())
734 }

push_response — the central decision

L735–L820

The most important function in the file. Everything the model says arrives here, and this is where the loop decides whether to continue.

Order matters, and the first two lines explain themselves:

  1. Record the frame — before validation, so debug shows what arrived even if it was garbage.
  2. Count the spend — before validation too. The comment is explicit: a malformed reply cost real tokens, and a retry loop that billed nothing would understate cost precisely when it is going wrong.
  3. Parse. On failure, hand off to retry_after.

Only a valid reply counts against the iteration budget — malformed ones consume retries instead, so a model stuck on syntax cannot silently eat the whole budget.

The final match is the routing table, in precedence order:

  • Response → the turn is over, back to Idle.
  • Over budget → stop, even for auto-approved reads. The comment puts it well: "free" is not "unbounded".
  • Read (without --confirm-reads) → run it now and continue, no modal.
  • Fetch (without --confirm-fetch) → park it for the event loop to spawn, no modal.
  • Edit → pre-flight through files::plan_edit. A hopeless edit goes straight back to the model; only a viable one reaches the modal, carrying its plan.
  • Everything else → wait for your approval.

The fetch arm sits below the max_iterations guard, with the read. Auto-approved does not mean unbudgeted: a model that fetches in a loop is exactly as stuck as one that runs commands in a loop, and "free" is about not interrupting you, not about being unbounded.

It is also the one arm that returns None without the turn having stopped. Idle and awaiting-approval both mean "nothing further happens until something external occurs"; here the something is a task the event loop is about to start. Status::Running is set so the UI shows the turn is still alive.

735 
736 /// Record a model reply, validating it against the protocol.
737 ///
738 /// The raw text goes into history either way: the model did say it, and
739 /// dropping it would leave two user turns adjacent.
740 /// Returns messages to send immediately, which happens when a malformed
741 /// reply earns a corrective retry.
742 pub fn push_response(&mut self, content: String, usage: Option<Usage>) -> Option<Vec<Message>> {
743 self.frame(Direction::Received, content.clone());
744 self.follow = true;
745 // Count the spend before validating: a malformed reply cost real tokens
746 // too, and a retry loop that billed nothing would badly understate it.
747 if let Some(usage) = &usage {
748 self.ledger.record(usage);
749 }
750 
751 let action = match protocol::parse_reply(&content) {
752 Ok(action) => action,
753 Err(err) => return self.retry_after(content, err),
754 };
755 
756 // Only a valid reply counts as progress against the loop budget.
757 self.iterations += 1;
758 self.retries = 0;
759 self.retry_anchor = None;
760 self.history.push(Message::assistant(content));
761 self.transcript.push(Entry::Action {
762 action: action.clone(),
763 usage,
764 });
765 
766 match action {
767 // A final answer ends the turn.
768 Action::Response(_) => self.status = Status::Idle,
769 // Any action past the loop budget stops rather than running, even the
770 // auto-approved ones — "free" is not "unbounded".
771 _ if self.iterations >= self.max_iterations => {
772 self.push_notice(format!(
773 "Stopped after {} model round-trips. Send another prompt to continue.",
774 self.iterations
775 ));
776 self.status = Status::Idle;
777 }
778 // A read mutates nothing and cannot leave the working directory, so it
779 // runs now and the loop continues without interrupting the user.
780 Action::Read { path } if !self.confirm_reads => {
781 return Some(self.perform_read(&path));
782 }
783 // A fetch is auto-approved on the same reasoning, but it is network
784 // I/O rather than a local read, so it cannot run inline here. Park
785 // it for `main` to spawn with the usual cancellation machinery.
786 Action::Fetch { url } if !self.confirm_fetches => {
787 self.pending_fetch = Some(url);
788 self.status = Status::Running;
789 self.follow = true;
790 }
791 // An edit is resolved against the file *before* the modal, so a
792 // hopeless one (no match, ambiguous) never bothers the user — it goes
793 // straight back to the model to fix.
794 Action::Edit { path, old, new } => {
795 let planned = match &self.sandbox {
796 Some(sandbox) => crate::files::plan_edit(sandbox, &path, &old, &new),
797 None => Err("file access is not configured".to_string()),
798 };
799 match planned {
800 Ok(plan) => {
801 self.status = Status::AwaitingApproval(Pending {
802 action: Action::Edit { path, old, new },
803 selected: Choice::Allow,
804 edit_plan: Some(plan),
805 });
806 }
807 Err(message) => return Some(self.push_edit_failure(&path, message)),
808 }
809 }
810 // Shell, write, and (under --confirm-reads) read wait for the user.
811 other => {
812 self.status = Status::AwaitingApproval(Pending {
813 action: other,
814 selected: Choice::Allow,
815 edit_plan: None,
816 });
817 }
818 }
819 None
820 }

push_edit_failure and perform_read

L821–L855

push_edit_failure reports a pre-flight failure as a WriteOutcome. That is not a hack: an edit executes as a write, so its failures are write failures, and reusing push_write_result keeps one path for framing, history, and the transcript entry.

perform_read is shared by the automatic path and the --confirm-reads approval path, so both behave identically. It runs synchronously — the doc comment justifies it: a bounded read from local disk is far cheaper than the task-spawning and generation-tagging a background job would need.

A failed read is reported to the model as a result, not raised as an error, so a bad path costs one round-trip instead of ending the turn.

821 
822 /// Report a pre-flight edit failure to the model. An edit runs as a write, so
823 /// its failure is a write result too — reusing [`App::push_write_result`]
824 /// keeps one path for framing, history, and the transcript entry.
825 fn push_edit_failure(&mut self, path: &str, message: String) -> Vec<Message> {
826 self.push_write_result(WriteOutcome {
827 path: path.to_string(),
828 bytes: 0,
829 error: Some(message),
830 timed_out: false,
831 cancelled: false,
832 })
833 }
834 
835 /// Read a file and hand the contents straight back to the model.
836 ///
837 /// Shared by the automatic path above and by the `--confirm-reads` approval
838 /// path, so both behave identically. Runs synchronously: a read is capped at
839 /// [`crate::files::MAX_READ_BYTES`] from local disk, which is far cheaper
840 /// than the task-spawning and generation-tagging a background job would need.
841 /// A failed read is reported to the model as a result, not raised as an
842 /// error, so a bad path costs one round-trip instead of ending the turn.
843 pub fn perform_read(&mut self, path: &str) -> Vec<Message> {
844 let outcome = match &self.sandbox {
845 Some(sandbox) => crate::files::read(sandbox, path),
846 None => ReadOutcome::failed(path, "file access is not configured"),
847 };
848 let encoded = protocol::encode_read_result(&outcome);
849 self.transcript.push(Entry::ReadResult(outcome));
850 self.frame(Direction::Sent, encoded.clone());
851 self.history.push(Message::user(encoded));
852 self.status = Status::Waiting;
853 self.follow = true;
854 self.history.clone()
855 }

retry_after — correct, or give up cleanly

L856–L913

The protocol-level retry loop, and the rollback at the end is the part worth understanding.

retry_anchor records where history was clean — before the first bad reply of this streak. While retrying, the bad reply and a targeted correction are appended, so the model can see what it did and what was wrong with it.

On giving up, history is truncated back to the anchor, rolling the whole failed exchange out of context.

Why roll it back rather than leave it: the comment says it plainly — leaving the model's own malformed output in context makes repeating it more likely. The transcript still shows what happened, so nothing is hidden from you; it is only hidden from the model.

The trailing user turn is popped too, matching push_error, so history ends on an assistant turn rather than two adjacent user turns — which some providers reject outright.

856 
857 /// Ask the model to try again after a protocol violation, or give up.
858 fn retry_after(
859 &mut self,
860 content: String,
861 error: protocol::ProtocolError,
862 ) -> Option<Vec<Message>> {
863 // Remember where context was clean, before the first bad reply.
864 if self.retry_anchor.is_none() {
865 self.retry_anchor = Some(self.history.len());
866 }
867 self.retries += 1;
868 self.transcript.push(Entry::Malformed {
869 reason: error.to_string(),
870 raw: content.clone(),
871 });
872 
873 if self.retries > self.max_retries {
874 // Roll the whole failed exchange out of context. Leaving the model's
875 // own malformed output behind makes repeating it more likely, and
876 // the transcript still shows what happened.
877 if let Some(anchor) = self.retry_anchor.take() {
878 self.history.truncate(anchor);
879 }
880 // Drop the trailing user turn too, matching `push_error`, so history
881 // ends on an assistant turn rather than two adjacent user turns.
882 if matches!(
883 self.history.last(),
884 Some(Message {
885 role: crate::openrouter::Role::User,
886 ..
887 })
888 ) {
889 self.history.pop();
890 }
891 self.retries = 0;
892 self.status = Status::Idle;
893 self.transcript.push(Entry::Error(format!(
894 "The model failed to follow the protocol after {} attempts. Giving up on this turn.",
895 self.max_retries
896 )));
897 return None;
898 }
899 
900 // Keep the bad reply plus a targeted correction, so the model can see
901 // what it did and what was wrong with it.
902 self.history.push(Message::assistant(content));
903 let correction = protocol::encode_correction(&error);
904 self.frame(Direction::Sent, correction.clone());
905 self.history.push(Message::user(correction));
906 self.push_notice(format!(
907 "Reply did not follow the protocol; retrying ({}/{}).",
908 self.retries, self.max_retries
909 ));
910 self.status = Status::Waiting;
911 Some(self.history.clone())
912 }
913 

toggle_choice, set_choice, approve

L914–L946

approve is where an edit becomes a write. If edit_plan is present, the returned action is Action::Write built from plan.updated — the contents computed during pre-flight.

Read the doc comment: the file is not re-read or re-matched after approval. That closes a real gap — otherwise the file could change between the diff you saw and the bytes that land.

set_choice exists for mouse hover, so moving the pointer over Deny focuses it and keyboard and mouse never disagree.

914 /// Move the focused button in the approval modal.
915 pub fn toggle_choice(&mut self) {
916 if let Status::AwaitingApproval(pending) = &mut self.status {
917 pending.selected = pending.selected.toggled();
918 }
919 }
920 
921 pub fn set_choice(&mut self, choice: Choice) {
922 if let Status::AwaitingApproval(pending) = &mut self.status {
923 pending.selected = choice;
924 }
925 }
926 
927 /// Accept the pending action; the caller runs it. Returns the action to run.
928 ///
929 /// An edit runs as the write its pre-flight prepared, so the bytes that land
930 /// are exactly the ones the diff showed — the file is not re-read or
931 /// re-matched after approval, which would open a window for it to change.
932 pub fn approve(&mut self) -> Option<Action> {
933 let Status::AwaitingApproval(pending) = &self.status else {
934 return None;
935 };
936 let action = match &pending.edit_plan {
937 Some(plan) => Action::Write {
938 path: plan.path.clone(),
939 contents: plan.updated.clone(),
940 },
941 None => pending.action.clone(),
942 };
943 self.status = Status::Running;
944 self.follow = true;
945 Some(action)
946 }

deny

L947–L970

Denial is communicated, not silent. It records what was refused, frames an <ai-harness-shell-result> saying so, and returns messages to send — so the model finds out and can propose something else rather than assuming its command ran.

The refused string is built per action type so the transcript shows the command text, or write path, or edit path.

The refusal label match is exhaustive, so adding Fetch to Action forced a line here. That is the intended pressure: a new action cannot be added without deciding what a denial of it says to the user.

947 
948 /// Refuse the pending action and tell the model, so it can try something
949 /// else rather than assuming it ran. Returns messages to send.
950 pub fn deny(&mut self) -> Option<Vec<Message>> {
951 let Status::AwaitingApproval(pending) = &self.status else {
952 return None;
953 };
954 // Show what was refused: the command, or the write's path.
955 let refused = match &pending.action {
956 Action::Shell(command) => command.clone(),
957 Action::Read { path } => format!("read {path}"),
958 Action::Fetch { url } => format!("fetch {url}"),
959 Action::Write { path, .. } => format!("write {path}"),
960 Action::Edit { path, .. } => format!("edit {path}"),
961 Action::Response(_) => String::new(),
962 };
963 self.transcript.push(Entry::Denied(refused));
964 let encoded = protocol::encode_denied();
965 self.frame(Direction::Sent, encoded.clone());
966 self.history.push(Message::user(encoded));
967 self.status = Status::Waiting;
968 self.follow = true;
969 Some(self.history.clone())
970 }

take_pending_fetch and the push_*_result family

L971–L1011

Twin functions with the identical five-step shape: encode, push a transcript entry, record the sent frame, append to history, set Waiting. Both return self.history.clone() unconditionally — a result always continues the loop.

Together with perform_read, push_fetch_result and deny, these are the five places the conversation goes back to the model without you typing anything.

take_pending_fetch is the other half of the outbox. Taking it clears it, which is what guarantees a parked fetch is spawned exactly once.

push_fetch_result is the same six lines as its siblings — encode, push an entry, frame, append to history, go back to Waiting, return the conversation. Every result in the harness re-enters the loop through this identical shape, which is why the loop has no loop construct anywhere.

971 
972 /// Record a finished command and hand the result back to the model.
973 pub fn push_command_result(&mut self, output: CommandOutput) -> Vec<Message> {
974 let encoded = protocol::encode_shell_result(&output);
975 self.transcript.push(Entry::CommandResult(Box::new(output)));
976 self.frame(Direction::Sent, encoded.clone());
977 self.history.push(Message::user(encoded));
978 self.status = Status::Waiting;
979 self.follow = true;
980 self.history.clone()
981 }
982 
983 /// Take the fetch the dispatch parked, if there is one.
984 ///
985 /// Called by the event loop after `push_response`, which cannot spawn the
986 /// work itself. Taking it clears it, so a fetch is spawned exactly once.
987 pub fn take_pending_fetch(&mut self) -> Option<String> {
988 self.pending_fetch.take()
989 }
990 
991 /// Record a finished fetch and hand the text back to the model.
992 pub fn push_fetch_result(&mut self, outcome: FetchOutcome) -> Vec<Message> {
993 let encoded = protocol::encode_fetch_result(&outcome);
994 self.transcript.push(Entry::FetchResult(Box::new(outcome)));
995 self.frame(Direction::Sent, encoded.clone());
996 self.history.push(Message::user(encoded));
997 self.status = Status::Waiting;
998 self.follow = true;
999 self.history.clone()
1000 }
1001 
1002 /// Record a finished write and hand the result back to the model.
1003 pub fn push_write_result(&mut self, outcome: WriteOutcome) -> Vec<Message> {
1004 let encoded = protocol::encode_write_result(&outcome.path, outcome.as_result());
1005 self.transcript.push(Entry::WriteResult(outcome));
1006 self.frame(Direction::Sent, encoded.clone());
1007 self.history.push(Message::user(encoded));
1008 self.status = Status::Waiting;
1009 self.follow = true;
1010 self.history.clone()
1011 }

push_error and reset_conversation

L1012–L1053

push_error drops the trailing user turn before recording the error, so a subsequent retry does not double-send the query or command result that failed.

reset_conversation (/clear and Ctrl+L) keeps only system messages — that retain is what preserves the protocol contract across a clear.

Note what it does not reset: ledger and prompt_history both survive, for the reasons given at their declarations.

The last three lines are the surprising behaviour, and the comment flags it: clear also overwrites the saved file — but only if one already exists, so a clear on a fresh session does not create one. Use /fork first to preserve.

1012 
1013 pub fn push_error(&mut self, message: String) {
1014 // Drop the trailing user turn (a query, or a command result) so a retry
1015 // does not double-send it.
1016 if matches!(
1017 self.history.last(),
1018 Some(Message {
1019 role: crate::openrouter::Role::User,
1020 ..
1021 })
1022 ) {
1023 self.history.pop();
1024 }
1025 self.transcript.push(Entry::Error(message));
1026 self.status = Status::Idle;
1027 self.follow = true;
1028 }
1029 
1030 pub fn push_notice(&mut self, message: impl Into<String>) {
1031 self.transcript.push(Entry::Notice(message.into()));
1032 self.follow = true;
1033 }
1034 
1035 /// Clear the conversation, keeping any system prompt in place.
1036 pub fn reset_conversation(&mut self) {
1037 self.history
1038 .retain(|m| m.role == crate::openrouter::Role::System);
1039 self.transcript.clear();
1040 self.scroll = 0;
1041 self.follow = true;
1042 self.iterations = 0;
1043 self.retries = 0;
1044 self.retry_anchor = None;
1045 self.status = Status::Idle;
1046 self.push_notice("Conversation cleared.");
1047 // "Clear" clears the file too: overwrite the current session with the
1048 // cleared state, but only if it was already saved (don't create a file
1049 // for a conversation that never began). Use /fork to preserve instead.
1050 if crate::session::exists(&self.sessions_dir, &self.current_session) {
1051 self.persist_current();
1052 }
1053 }

scrolling

L1054–L1071

Three one-liners implementing the follow behaviour. scroll_up always detaches (follow = false); scroll_down re-attaches automatically once it reaches the bottom.

That auto-reattach is why the README can say scrolling back down resumes following without you pressing End — though End (scroll_to_bottom) is there for the impatient.

max is passed in rather than stored because it depends on the rendered height, which only ui.rs knows — it comes back through Metrics each frame.

1054 
1055 pub fn scroll_up(&mut self, rows: u16) {
1056 self.scroll = self.scroll.saturating_sub(rows);
1057 self.follow = false;
1058 }
1059 
1060 pub fn scroll_down(&mut self, rows: u16, max: u16) {
1061 self.scroll = (self.scroll + rows).min(max);
1062 if self.scroll >= max {
1063 self.follow = true;
1064 }
1065 }
1066 
1067 pub fn scroll_to_bottom(&mut self, max: u16) {
1068 self.scroll = max;
1069 self.follow = true;
1070 }
1071}

What the tests cover

1,822 lines across two modules — mod tests and mod file_tests — and they are the reason this file can be refactored with confidence. Being pure state, they need no mocks: construct an App, push a reply, assert on the resulting status, history, and transcript.

The heavily covered areas are the ones with the most branching: the retry path (each retry preserves the bad reply plus a correction; giving up truncates history back to retry_anchor and drops the trailing user turn), the iteration budget (an action past the budget stops rather than running, including auto-approved reads), prompt recall (editing a recalled entry ends navigation), and session save/clear/fork interactions.

mod file_tests covers the read and edit paths against a real temporary directory, including the pre-flight rejection that never reaches the modal.

ui.rs

815 lines of code · 914 lines of tests

All rendering. Lays out the frame, draws the transcript, the two modals, the status bar and the prompt — and measures the geometry the event loop needs back.

uses app, protocol::Action, wrap, ratatui

used by main

Read-mostly: with one deliberate exception it takes &App and produces pixels. The exception is draw_transcript, which writes app.scroll — because the correct scroll offset cannot be known until the content has been wrapped, and this is the only place that happens.

The idea that ties the file together is Metrics. Rendering measures things — how tall the wrapped transcript turned out, where the Allow and Deny buttons landed, which rows the session picker occupies — and returns them. main.rs then uses those numbers for mouse hit-testing and scroll clamping, so the two files never have to independently agree on layout maths.

The other recurring principle: wrap up front, never let ratatui do it. One Line is exactly one screen row, which is what makes lines.len() the true rendered height. Scroll clamping and stick-to-bottom both depend on that being exact.

Layout is four vertical bands: transcript (flexible), completion menu (0 rows when closed), status (1 row), prompt (grows to 10 rows). Modals are drawn last, on top.

imports and constants

L1–L15

MAX_INPUT_ROWS = 10 caps the prompt box; past that it scrolls internally rather than eating the screen.

SPINNER is eight braille frames. It is indexed by app.tick / 2 in transcript_lines, so at the 80 ms tick rate it advances every 160 ms — fast enough to look alive, slow enough not to strobe.

1//! Rendering. The prompt is pinned to the bottom; the transcript takes the rest.
2 
3use ratatui::Frame;
4use ratatui::layout::{Constraint, Layout, Position, Rect};
5use ratatui::style::{Color, Modifier, Style, Stylize};
6use ratatui::text::{Line, Span, Text};
7use ratatui::widgets::{Block, Clear, Paragraph};
8 
9use crate::app::{App, Choice, Direction, Entry, Pending, Status};
10use crate::protocol::Action;
11use crate::wrap;
12 
13/// Prompt box grows with the text, up to this many rows of content.
14const MAX_INPUT_ROWS: u16 = 10;
15const SPINNER: [&str; 8] = ["⠋", "⠙", "⠹", "⠸", "⠼", "⠴", "⠦", "⠧"];

struct Metrics and fn hit

L16–L46

The channel back to the event loop. Everything here is something only the renderer can know.

max_scroll() — content height minus viewport height — is the single definition of "how far down can you scroll", used by App::scroll_down, PageDown, and the mouse wheel alike. saturating_sub handles content shorter than the viewport, giving 0 rather than underflowing.

hit is plain rectangle containment, used for the modal buttons and the picker list.

16 
17/// How the last frame was laid out. The event loop needs this to clamp
18/// scrolling to the content that was actually rendered.
19#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
20pub struct Metrics {
21 pub transcript_height: u16,
22 pub content_height: u16,
23 /// Button areas from the approval modal, for mouse hit-testing. `None` when
24 /// the modal is not up.
25 pub allow_button: Option<Rect>,
26 pub deny_button: Option<Rect>,
27 /// The session picker's row area and the index of its first visible row, so
28 /// a click can be mapped back to a session. `None` when the picker is closed.
29 pub picker_list: Option<Rect>,
30 pub picker_offset: usize,
31}
32 
33/// Did `(column, row)` land inside `area`?
34pub fn hit(area: Option<Rect>, column: u16, row: u16) -> bool {
35 area.is_some_and(|a| {
36 column >= a.x && column < a.x + a.width && row >= a.y && row < a.y + a.height
37 })
38}
39 
40impl Metrics {
41 /// Largest valid scroll offset: the point where the last line sits at the
42 /// bottom of the viewport.
43 pub fn max_scroll(&self) -> u16 {
44 self.content_height.saturating_sub(self.transcript_height)
45 }
46}

fn draw — the frame

L47–L93

The layout decisions, in a specific order for a reason: the prompt is laid out first, before any area is allocated, because its height depends on the wrapped text and the transcript gets whatever is left.

input_width = width - 4 accounts for 2 border columns and the 2-column "> " gutter — get this wrong and the cursor drifts from the text.

The completion menu sits above the status line, so it grows toward the transcript and the prompt never moves under your fingers. It is capped at half the screen so it cannot push the prompt off a short terminal — which is exactly why draw_completions has to scroll internally.

Modals are drawn last so they sit on top, and the two are mutually exclusive with approval taking precedence.

47 
48pub fn draw(frame: &mut Frame, app: &mut App) -> Metrics {
49 let area = frame.area();
50 
51 // Lay the prompt out first so we know how tall it needs to be.
52 // -2 for the box borders, -2 for the "> " gutter.
53 let input_width = area.width.saturating_sub(4).max(1);
54 let input_layout = app.input.layout(input_width);
55 let input_rows = (input_layout.rows.len() as u16).clamp(1, MAX_INPUT_ROWS);
56 
57 // The completion menu sits directly above the status line, so it grows
58 // towards the transcript and leaves the prompt where it is.
59 let completions = app.completions();
60 let menu_rows = if completions.is_empty() {
61 0
62 } else {
63 (completions.len() as u16 + 2).min(area.height / 2)
64 };
65 
66 let [transcript_area, menu_area, status_area, input_area] = Layout::vertical([
67 Constraint::Min(1),
68 Constraint::Length(menu_rows),
69 Constraint::Length(1),
70 Constraint::Length(input_rows + 2),
71 ])
72 .areas(area);
73 
74 let mut metrics = draw_transcript(frame, app, transcript_area);
75 if menu_rows > 0 {
76 draw_completions(frame, &completions, app.completion_index(), menu_area);
77 }
78 draw_status(frame, app, status_area);
79 draw_input(frame, app, input_area, &input_layout, input_rows);
80 
81 // Drawn last so it sits above everything else. The two modals are mutually
82 // exclusive; approval takes precedence if both were ever set.
83 if let Some(pending) = app.pending() {
84 let (allow, deny) = draw_approval(frame, pending, area);
85 metrics.allow_button = Some(allow);
86 metrics.deny_button = Some(deny);
87 } else if let Some(picker) = app.picker() {
88 let (list, offset) = draw_picker(frame, picker, area);
89 metrics.picker_list = Some(list);
90 metrics.picker_offset = offset;
91 }
92 metrics
93}

fn draw_picker — the /load overlay

L94–L153

A centred, bordered box sized to the session list and capped at half the screen height.

frame.render_widget(Clear, modal) is the ratatui idiom for a modal: blank the region first, or the transcript shows through.

The offset calculation is the scroll window that keeps the selection visible in a long list — the same expression appears in draw_completions, and both are written as a saturating_sub then min pair so they cannot go negative or run past the end.

Returning (list_area, offset) is what makes the list clickable: main::picker_row_at needs both to turn a mouse row into a session index.

94 
95/// The `/load` session picker. Returns the inner row area and the index of the
96/// first visible row, so a click can be mapped back to a session.
97fn draw_picker(frame: &mut Frame, picker: &crate::app::Picker, area: Rect) -> (Rect, usize) {
98 let width = area.width.saturating_sub(8).clamp(20, 60);
99 // Border (2) + footer (1) + a blank (1), plus one row per session, capped.
100 let max_list = (area.height.saturating_sub(2) / 2).max(1);
101 let list_rows = (picker.sessions.len() as u16).clamp(1, max_list);
102 let height = list_rows + 4;
103 
104 let modal = center(area, width, height);
105 frame.render_widget(Clear, modal);
106 let block = Block::bordered()
107 .title(Line::from(" load session ").bold())
108 .border_style(Style::default().fg(Color::Blue));
109 let inner = block.inner(modal);
110 frame.render_widget(block, modal);
111 
112 let [list_area, footer_area] =
113 Layout::vertical([Constraint::Min(1), Constraint::Length(1)]).areas(inner);
114 
115 // Scroll a window around the selection so it stays visible in a long list.
116 let visible = list_area.height as usize;
117 let offset = picker
118 .selected
119 .saturating_sub(visible.saturating_sub(1))
120 .min(picker.sessions.len().saturating_sub(visible));
121 
122 let rows: Vec<Line> = picker
123 .sessions
124 .iter()
125 .enumerate()
126 .skip(offset)
127 .take(visible)
128 .map(|(i, name)| {
129 let focused = i == picker.selected;
130 let style = if focused {
131 Style::default()
132 .fg(Color::Black)
133 .bg(Color::Blue)
134 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)
135 } else {
136 Style::default().fg(Color::Gray)
137 };
138 let marker = if focused { "› " } else { " " };
139 Line::from(Span::styled(format!("{marker}{name}"), style))
140 })
141 .collect();
142 frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new(Text::from(rows)), list_area);
143 
144 frame.render_widget(
145 Paragraph::new(Line::from(Span::styled(
146 "↑/↓ choose · Enter load · Esc cancel",
147 Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray),
148 ))),
149 footer_area,
150 );
151 
152 (list_area, offset)
153}

fn draw_completions

L154–L208

The slash-command menu. Descriptions are aligned into a column by measuring the longest name, so it reads as a table.

Read the comment at lines 172–175 — it explains a consequence rather than a mechanism. The menu is capped so it cannot push the prompt off a short screen, which means the list can outgrow it; without internal scrolling, entries past the cap would be invisible and unreachable, since ↑/↓ wrap through all of them.

154 
155/// The slash-command completion menu, shown above the status line.
156fn draw_completions(
157 frame: &mut Frame,
158 completions: &[&'static crate::command::Spec],
159 selected: usize,
160 area: Rect,
161) {
162 frame.render_widget(Clear, area);
163 let block = Block::bordered()
164 .title(Line::from(" commands ").bold())
165 .border_style(Style::default().fg(Color::Blue));
166 let inner = block.inner(area);
167 frame.render_widget(block, area);
168 
169 // Align descriptions into a column so the list reads as a table.
170 let name_width = completions.iter().map(|c| c.name.len()).max().unwrap_or(0);
171 
172 // The menu is capped so it cannot push the prompt off a short screen, which
173 // means the list can outgrow it. Scroll a window around the selection — the
174 // same treatment `draw_picker` gives a long session list — or entries past
175 // the cap would be invisible and unreachable.
176 let visible = inner.height as usize;
177 let offset = selected
178 .saturating_sub(visible.saturating_sub(1))
179 .min(completions.len().saturating_sub(visible));
180 
181 let lines: Vec<Line> = completions
182 .iter()
183 .enumerate()
184 .skip(offset)
185 .take(visible)
186 .map(|(i, spec)| {
187 let focused = i == selected;
188 let name = format!(" /{:<name_width$} ", spec.name, name_width = name_width);
189 let name_style = if focused {
190 Style::default()
191 .fg(Color::Black)
192 .bg(Color::Blue)
193 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)
194 } else {
195 Style::default().fg(Color::Blue)
196 };
197 Line::from(vec![
198 Span::styled(name, name_style),
199 Span::styled(
200 format!(" {}", spec.description),
201 Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray),
202 ),
203 ])
204 })
205 .collect();
206 
207 frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new(Text::from(lines)), inner);
208}

fn draw_approval — the modal

L209–L332

The longest function in the file, and the one you look at most often in practice.

The opening match picks a prompt, title, and body per action type, and the body treatment differs by what could be huge:

  • Read — just the path. Only reachable under --confirm-reads.
  • Write — path plus a bounded preview, so a large file cannot blow up the box.
  • Edit — path plus a -/+ diff. This is the payoff of pre-flighting the edit: what you see is exactly what will be applied.
  • Shell — the command in full. A command is short and you must read all of it before approving.

Height is body + 7, clamped to the screen and floored at 7, so the buttons are always on screen no matter what.

The button loop draws both from one array. The focused one gets [Allow] brackets and a background colour — belt and braces, so focus is visible on terminals with poor colour support. Returning the two Rects is what makes them clickable.

The fetch arm exists so the --confirm-fetch modal shows the URL under its own heading instead of falling through to the shell-styled default and announcing "the model wants to run". If you have turned this modal on, the URL is the decision — it is the whole thing you are being asked to approve.

209 
210/// The approval modal. Returns the Allow and Deny button areas so the event
211/// loop can hit-test mouse clicks against them.
212fn draw_approval(frame: &mut Frame, pending: &Pending, area: Rect) -> (Rect, Rect) {
213 let width = area.width.saturating_sub(8).clamp(24, 76);
214 
215 // Build the body: a command shown in full, or a write shown as path + a
216 // bounded preview so a large file never blows up the box.
217 let inner_width = width.saturating_sub(4) as usize;
218 let (prompt, title, mut body): (&str, &str, Vec<Line>) = match &pending.action {
219 // Only reachable under `--confirm-reads`; reads are otherwise silent.
220 Action::Read { path } => (
221 "The model wants to read:",
222 " read this file? ",
223 vec![Line::from(Span::styled(
224 path.clone(),
225 Style::default()
226 .fg(Color::Blue)
227 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
228 ))],
229 ),
230 // Only reachable under `--confirm-fetch`; fetches are otherwise silent.
231 Action::Fetch { url } => (
232 "The model wants to fetch:",
233 " fetch this URL? ",
234 vec![Line::from(Span::styled(
235 url.clone(),
236 Style::default()
237 .fg(Color::Blue)
238 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
239 ))],
240 ),
241 Action::Write { path, contents } => (
242 "The model wants to write:",
243 " write this file? ",
244 std::iter::once(Line::from(Span::styled(
245 path.clone(),
246 Style::default()
247 .fg(Color::Cyan)
248 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
249 )))
250 .chain(preview_lines(contents, inner_width))
251 .collect(),
252 ),
253 Action::Edit { path, old, new } => (
254 "The model wants to edit:",
255 " apply this edit? ",
256 std::iter::once(Line::from(Span::styled(
257 path.clone(),
258 Style::default()
259 .fg(Color::Cyan)
260 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
261 )))
262 .chain(diff_lines(old, new, inner_width))
263 .collect(),
264 ),
265 action => (
266 "The model wants to run:",
267 " run this command? ",
268 body_lines(
269 action.body(),
270 Style::default()
271 .fg(Color::Magenta)
272 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
273 inner_width,
274 ),
275 ),
276 };
277 
278 // Border + prompt + blank + body + blank + buttons.
279 let height = (body.len() as u16 + 7)
280 .min(area.height.saturating_sub(2))
281 .max(7);
282 let modal = center(area, width, height);
283 frame.render_widget(Clear, modal);
284 
285 let block = Block::bordered()
286 .title(Line::from(title).bold())
287 .border_style(Style::default().fg(Color::Yellow));
288 let inner = block.inner(modal);
289 frame.render_widget(block, modal);
290 
291 let [text_area, button_area] =
292 Layout::vertical([Constraint::Min(1), Constraint::Length(1)]).areas(inner);
293 
294 let mut lines = vec![Line::from(Span::styled(
295 prompt,
296 Style::default().fg(Color::Gray),
297 ))];
298 lines.push(Line::default());
299 lines.append(&mut body);
300 frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new(Text::from(lines)), text_area);
301 
302 // Two fixed-width buttons, centred as a pair.
303 const BUTTON: u16 = 11;
304 let gap = 2;
305 let total = BUTTON * 2 + gap;
306 let start = button_area.x + button_area.width.saturating_sub(total) / 2;
307 let allow = Rect::new(start, button_area.y, BUTTON, 1);
308 let deny = Rect::new(start + BUTTON + gap, button_area.y, BUTTON, 1);
309 
310 for (rect, label, choice, colour) in [
311 (allow, " Allow ", Choice::Allow, Color::Green),
312 (deny, " Deny ", Choice::Deny, Color::Red),
313 ] {
314 let focused = pending.selected == choice;
315 let style = if focused {
316 Style::default()
317 .fg(Color::Black)
318 .bg(colour)
319 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)
320 } else {
321 Style::default().fg(colour)
322 };
323 let text = if focused {
324 format!("[{label}]")
325 } else {
326 format!(" {label} ")
327 };
328 frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new(Line::from(Span::styled(text, style))), rect);
329 }
330 
331 (allow, deny)
332}

fn center

L333–L344

Centres a box, clamping both dimensions to the available area first — which is what stops the subtraction on the next lines from underflowing on a terminal smaller than the requested modal.

333 
334/// Centre a `width` x `height` box inside `area`.
335fn center(area: Rect, width: u16, height: u16) -> Rect {
336 let width = width.min(area.width);
337 let height = height.min(area.height);
338 Rect::new(
339 area.x + (area.width - width) / 2,
340 area.y + (area.height - height) / 2,
341 width,
342 height,
343 )
344}

fn draw_transcript

L345–L376

Small, but it holds the file's central mechanism.

The comment at 341 is the one to read: wrapping up front means lines.len() is the true rendered height, which is what both scroll clamping and stick-to-bottom depend on. Hand unwrapped text to Paragraph and it wraps internally, and its height becomes unknowable.

The app.follow branch is the one mutation in the file, and it can only happen here — "pin to the bottom" is not resolvable until the wrapped height is known. The else arm re-clamps a stale offset, which is what keeps the view sane when the terminal is resized.

345 
346fn draw_transcript(frame: &mut Frame, app: &mut App, area: Rect) -> Metrics {
347 let block = Block::bordered()
348 .title(Line::from(" ai-harness ").bold())
349 .border_style(Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray));
350 let inner = block.inner(area);
351 
352 // Wrapping up front means `lines.len()` is the true rendered height, which
353 // is what scroll clamping and "stick to the bottom" both depend on.
354 let lines = transcript_lines(app, inner.width as usize);
355 let content_height = lines.len() as u16;
356 let metrics = Metrics {
357 transcript_height: inner.height,
358 content_height,
359 ..Metrics::default()
360 };
361 
362 // Following means "pin to the bottom", which we can only resolve here,
363 // once we know how tall the wrapped content turned out to be.
364 let max_scroll = metrics.max_scroll();
365 if app.follow {
366 app.scroll = max_scroll;
367 } else {
368 app.scroll = app.scroll.min(max_scroll);
369 }
370 
371 let paragraph = Paragraph::new(Text::from(lines))
372 .block(block)
373 .scroll((app.scroll, 0));
374 frame.render_widget(paragraph, area);
375 metrics
376}

fn transcript_lines

L377–L435

Assembles the whole transcript. Three parts: an empty-state hint, the entries, and the live tail.

The per-entry loop renders into a scratch block first and skips it if empty. That is what makes a hidden frame contribute nothing at all — not even the blank separator line — so toggling /debug off leaves no gaps behind.

The tail is either the streaming reply or the spinner, never both. The streamed text gets a ▌ block cursor appended to signal it is still arriving; when the reply completes, finish_stream clears it and the committed Entry::Action takes its place.

377 
378/// Build the transcript as already-wrapped lines, so one `Line` is one screen row.
379fn transcript_lines(app: &App, width: usize) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
380 let mut lines: Vec<Line> = Vec::new();
381 
382 if app.transcript.is_empty() {
383 lines.extend(body_lines(
384 "Type a prompt and press Enter. Alt+Enter inserts a newline; Ctrl+C quits.",
385 Style::default()
386 .fg(Color::DarkGray)
387 .add_modifier(Modifier::ITALIC),
388 width,
389 ));
390 }
391 
392 for entry in app.transcript.iter() {
393 // Rendered per entry so a hidden one contributes nothing at all — not
394 // even the blank separator line.
395 let mut block: Vec<Line> = Vec::new();
396 render_entry(app, entry, width, &mut block);
397 if block.is_empty() {
398 continue;
399 }
400 if !lines.is_empty() {
401 lines.push(Line::default());
402 }
403 lines.extend(block);
404 }
405 
406 // The live reply renders in place of the spinner once tokens arrive.
407 if let Some(text) = &app.streaming {
408 lines.push(Line::default());
409 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
410 app.model.clone(),
411 Style::default()
412 .fg(Color::Green)
413 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
414 )));
415 // A block cursor on the last line signals the reply is still arriving.
416 let mut body = body_lines(&format!("{text}▌"), Style::default(), width);
417 lines.append(&mut body);
418 } else {
419 let activity = match app.status {
420 Status::Waiting => Some("thinking…"),
421 Status::Running => Some("running…"),
422 _ => None,
423 };
424 if let Some(activity) = activity {
425 let spinner = SPINNER[(app.tick / 2) % SPINNER.len()];
426 lines.push(Line::default());
427 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
428 format!("{spinner} {activity}"),
429 Style::default().fg(Color::Yellow),
430 )));
431 }
432 }
433 
434 lines
435}

render_entry — user turns and actions

L436–L505

The Action arm is the most designed part of the display, and the comment at 438 says why: labelling the action type is the whole point of the protocol — you should be able to see which of the six branches the model chose, at a glance, by colour and word.

The header is built up in layers: label, then the path for a write or edit, then the model name, then token counts if usage came back.

The body switches on the same action again, because each wants different treatment: a command shown as a command, a read showing just its path (contents arrive later as a result), a response as prose, a write as a bounded preview, and an edit as a diff.

A fetch is labelled in blue alongside read, not in magenta with shell. The colour is carrying the approval story: blue for the things that happened without asking you, magenta and cyan for the things you agreed to.

436 
437fn render_entry(app: &App, entry: &Entry, width: usize, lines: &mut Vec<Line<'static>>) {
438 match entry {
439 Entry::User(content) => {
440 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
441 "you",
442 Style::default()
443 .fg(Color::Cyan)
444 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
445 )));
446 lines.extend(body_lines(content, Style::default(), width));
447 }
448 Entry::Action { action, usage } => {
449 // Label the action type, since that is the whole point of the
450 // protocol: the user should see which branch the model chose.
451 let (label, colour) = match action {
452 Action::Shell(_) => ("shell", Color::Magenta),
453 Action::Read { .. } => ("read", Color::Blue),
454 Action::Fetch { .. } => ("fetch", Color::Blue),
455 Action::Write { .. } => ("write", Color::Cyan),
456 Action::Edit { .. } => ("edit", Color::Cyan),
457 Action::Response(_) => ("response", Color::Green),
458 };
459 let mut header = vec![Span::styled(
460 label,
461 Style::default().fg(colour).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
462 )];
463 // For a write or edit, the path is the headline; the body is below.
464 if let Action::Write { path, .. } | Action::Edit { path, .. } = action {
465 header.push(Span::styled(
466 format!(" {path}"),
467 Style::default().fg(Color::Cyan),
468 ));
469 }
470 header.push(Span::styled(
471 format!(" {}", app.model),
472 Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray),
473 ));
474 if let Some(u) = usage {
475 header.push(Span::styled(
476 format!(" {} in / {} out", u.prompt_tokens, u.completion_tokens),
477 Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray),
478 ));
479 }
480 lines.push(Line::from(header));
481 
482 match action {
483 // Shell commands read as commands, not prose.
484 Action::Shell(cmd) => {
485 lines.extend(body_lines(cmd, Style::default().fg(Color::Magenta), width))
486 }
487 // The path is the whole action; the contents arrive as a result.
488 Action::Read { path } => {
489 lines.extend(body_lines(path, Style::default().fg(Color::Blue), width))
490 }
491 // Likewise the URL; the page text arrives as a result.
492 Action::Fetch { url } => {
493 lines.extend(body_lines(url, Style::default().fg(Color::Blue), width))
494 }
495 Action::Response(text) => lines.extend(body_lines(text, Style::default(), width)),
496 // A file could be huge; show a bounded preview, not the whole thing.
497 Action::Write { contents, .. } => {
498 lines.extend(preview_lines(contents, width));
499 }
500 // An edit reads as a diff: what goes, what comes.
501 Action::Edit { old, new, .. } => {
502 lines.extend(diff_lines(old, new, width));
503 }
504 }
505 }

render_entry — results

L506–L619

The four result variants share a shape: a result label coloured by success, a summary, then details.

Malformed shows the parser's reason and the raw text the model actually sent — which is the difference between "something went wrong" and being able to see the stray sentence that broke it.

Command results print stdout dim and stderr red, each only if non-empty, and append an explicit truncation marker so silence is never ambiguous.

Read results get an interesting comment at 552: the model receives the whole file, but the transcript shows only a taste — because a read happened without you asking for it. The counts in the header tell you the size.

The FetchResult arm mirrors ReadResult, with one addition — when redirects moved the request, the landing URL is shown on its own line.

Why that line is worth the space: for every other action in the transcript you approved the exact thing that ran. A fetch happened without you, so where it actually ended up is not a detail — it is the part you would want to notice.
506 Entry::Malformed { reason, raw } => {
507 lines.push(Line::from(vec![
508 Span::styled(
509 "protocol error",
510 Style::default()
511 .fg(Color::Yellow)
512 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
513 ),
514 Span::styled(format!(" {reason}"), Style::default().fg(Color::Yellow)),
515 ]));
516 lines.extend(body_lines(raw, Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray), width));
517 }
518 Entry::CommandResult(output) => {
519 let ok = output.succeeded();
520 lines.push(Line::from(vec![
521 Span::styled(
522 "result",
523 Style::default()
524 .fg(if ok { Color::Blue } else { Color::Red })
525 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
526 ),
527 Span::styled(
528 format!(" {}", output.summary()),
529 Style::default().fg(if ok { Color::DarkGray } else { Color::Red }),
530 ),
531 ]));
532 let dim = Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray);
533 if !output.stdout.trim().is_empty() {
534 lines.extend(body_lines(output.stdout.trim_end(), dim, width));
535 }
536 if !output.stderr.trim().is_empty() {
537 lines.extend(body_lines(
538 output.stderr.trim_end(),
539 Style::default().fg(Color::Red),
540 width,
541 ));
542 }
543 if output.truncated {
544 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
545 "… output truncated",
546 dim.add_modifier(Modifier::ITALIC),
547 )));
548 }
549 }
550 Entry::ReadResult(outcome) => {
551 let ok = outcome.succeeded();
552 lines.push(Line::from(vec![
553 Span::styled(
554 "result",
555 Style::default()
556 .fg(if ok { Color::Blue } else { Color::Red })
557 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
558 ),
559 Span::styled(
560 format!(" {} {}", outcome.path, outcome.summary()),
561 Style::default().fg(if ok { Color::DarkGray } else { Color::Red }),
562 ),
563 ]));
564 match &outcome.error {
565 Some(error) => {
566 lines.extend(body_lines(error, Style::default().fg(Color::Red), width))
567 }
568 // The model gets the whole file; the transcript gets a taste of
569 // it, since a read happens without the user asking for it. The
570 // counts are already in the header above.
571 None => lines.extend(preview_body(&outcome.contents, width)),
572 }
573 }
574 Entry::FetchResult(outcome) => {
575 let ok = outcome.succeeded();
576 lines.push(Line::from(vec![
577 Span::styled(
578 "result",
579 Style::default()
580 .fg(if ok { Color::Blue } else { Color::Red })
581 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
582 ),

585 Style::default().fg(if ok { Color::DarkGray } else { Color::Red }),
586 ),
587 ]));

601 }

609 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
