render_entry — denied, frames, errors, notices

L620–L671

Denied renders the refused command struck through, which reads at a glance as "this did not run".

The two Frame arms are the /debug mechanism: the first is guarded on app.debug, the second is a catch-all that produces no lines at all. Recorded always, displayed conditionally — which is what makes /debug reveal traffic that already happened rather than only what comes next.

Notice has no label — it is italic grey body text, deliberately quieter than everything else, since notices are housekeeping.

620 Entry::Denied(command) => {
621 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
622 "denied",
623 Style::default().fg(Color::Red).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
624 )));
625 lines.extend(body_lines(
626 command,
627 Style::default()
628 .fg(Color::DarkGray)
629 .add_modifier(Modifier::CROSSED_OUT),
630 width,
631 ));
632 }
633 // Recorded always, shown only in debug mode, so toggling /debug
634 // reveals traffic that already happened.
635 Entry::Frame { direction, body } if app.debug => {
636 let label = match direction {
637 Direction::Sent => "sent",
638 Direction::Received => "received",
639 };
640 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
641 format!("{} {label}", direction.arrow()),
642 Style::default()
643 .fg(Color::Yellow)
644 .add_modifier(Modifier::DIM | Modifier::BOLD),
645 )));
646 lines.extend(body_lines(
647 body,
648 Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray),
649 width,
650 ));
651 }
652 // Frames stay hidden outside debug mode, contributing no lines.
653 Entry::Frame { .. } => {}
654 Entry::Error(message) => {
655 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
656 "error",
657 Style::default().fg(Color::Red).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
658 )));
659 lines.extend(body_lines(message, Style::default().fg(Color::Red), width));
660 }
661 Entry::Notice(message) => {
662 lines.extend(body_lines(
663 message,
664 Style::default()
665 .fg(Color::DarkGray)
666 .add_modifier(Modifier::ITALIC),
667 width,
668 ));
669 }
670 }
671}

body_lines, preview_lines, preview_body

L672–L713

The three text helpers. body_lines is the workhorse: wrap through wrap::text and style each row, so every caller gets one Line per screen row.

preview_body caps at 8 lines with a "… N more line(s)" marker. preview_lines adds a size header on top — the split exists because some callers (the read result) already print the counts in their own header and would otherwise show them twice.

672 
673fn body_lines(content: &str, style: Style, width: usize) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
674 wrap::text(content, width)
675 .into_iter()
676 .map(|row| Line::from(Span::styled(row, style)))
677 .collect()
678}
679 
680/// The first few lines of file contents, plus a size summary — so a large write
681/// never floods the transcript or the approval modal.
682fn preview_lines(contents: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
683 let dim = Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray);
684 let mut lines = vec![Line::from(Span::styled(
685 format!(
686 "{} line(s), {} bytes",
687 contents.lines().count(),
688 contents.len()
689 ),
690 dim.add_modifier(Modifier::ITALIC),
691 ))];
692 lines.extend(preview_body(contents, width));
693 lines
694}
695 
696/// Just the bounded excerpt, for callers whose header already carries the size.
697fn preview_body(contents: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
698 const MAX: usize = 8;
699 let total = contents.lines().count();
700 let dim = Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray);
701 
702 let mut lines: Vec<Line> = Vec::new();
703 for line in contents.lines().take(MAX) {
704 lines.extend(body_lines(line, dim, width));
705 }
706 if total > MAX {
707 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
708 format!("… {} more line(s)", total - MAX),
709 dim.add_modifier(Modifier::ITALIC),
710 )));
711 }
712 lines
713}

fn diff_lines — what an edit will do

L714–L762

Renders an edit as a unified diff: removed lines red with -, added lines green with +. Each side capped at 6 lines.

The nested side function handles one side. The detail worth noticing is cont = " ": when a long line wraps, the continuation is indented to line up under the text rather than under the marker, so a wrapped removal cannot be misread as two separate removed lines.

The empty-new branch prints + (deleted) explicitly. An empty <ai-harness-new> is a legitimate deletion, and showing nothing would look like a rendering bug at the exact moment you are deciding whether to approve destroying a span of a file.

714 
715/// A unified diff of an edit: removed lines in red with `-`, added lines in
716/// green with `+`. Each side is capped like a preview so a large edit never
717/// blows up the modal or the transcript.
718fn diff_lines(old: &str, new: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<Line<'static>> {
719 const MAX: usize = 6;
720 
721 fn side(text: &str, marker: char, colour: Color, width: usize, lines: &mut Vec<Line<'static>>) {
722 // Line up wrapped continuations under the text, not the marker.
723 let cont = " ";
724 let inner = width.saturating_sub(2).max(1);
725 let total = text.lines().count();
726 for line in text.lines().take(MAX) {
727 let wrapped = wrap::text(line, inner);
728 for (i, row) in wrapped.into_iter().enumerate() {
729 let prefix = if i == 0 {
730 format!("{marker} ")
731 } else {
732 cont.to_string()
733 };
734 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
735 format!("{prefix}{row}"),
736 Style::default().fg(colour),
737 )));
738 }
739 }
740 if total > MAX {
741 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
742 format!("{marker} … {} more line(s)", total - MAX),
743 Style::default().fg(colour).add_modifier(Modifier::ITALIC),
744 )));
745 }
746 }
747 
748 let mut lines = Vec::new();
749 side(old, '-', Color::Red, width, &mut lines);
750 // An empty replacement is a deletion; say so rather than showing nothing.
751 if new.is_empty() {
752 lines.push(Line::from(Span::styled(
753 "+ (deleted)",
754 Style::default()
755 .fg(Color::Green)
756 .add_modifier(Modifier::ITALIC),
757 )));
758 } else {
759 side(new, '+', Color::Green, width, &mut lines);
760 }
761 lines
762}

fn draw_status

L763–L814

The one-line bar: a coloured state chip, the model, then optional segments.

Cost appears only once something has been spent, so a fresh session does not open with a row of zeroes. The scrolled — End to resume hint appears only when detached, which is what makes the detached state discoverable rather than confusing.

The key hints are context-sensitive, and this is the nicest touch in the file: with a modal up they describe the modal's keys; while busy they show the one useful key (Esc); otherwise they show the editing keys. The bar never advertises a key that would do nothing right now.

763 
764fn draw_status(frame: &mut Frame, app: &App, area: Rect) {
765 let (label, colour) = match app.status {
766 Status::Idle => (" ready ", Color::Green),
767 Status::Waiting => (" waiting ", Color::Yellow),
768 Status::Streaming => (" streaming ", Color::Cyan),
769 Status::AwaitingApproval(_) => (" approve ", Color::Magenta),
770 Status::Running => (" running ", Color::Blue),
771 };
772 
773 let mut spans = vec![
774 Span::styled(label, Style::default().fg(Color::Black).bg(colour)),
775 Span::raw(" "),
776 Span::styled(app.model.clone(), Style::default().fg(Color::Gray)),
777 ];
778 // Cumulative spend, once there is any. Hidden on a fresh session so the bar
779 // does not open with a row of zeroes.
780 if !app.ledger.is_empty() {
781 spans.push(Span::styled(
782 format!(" {}", app.cost_status()),
783 Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray),
784 ));
785 }
786 if app.debug {
787 spans.push(Span::styled(
788 " debug",
789 Style::default()
790 .fg(Color::Yellow)
791 .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
792 ));
793 }
794 if !app.follow {
795 spans.push(Span::styled(
796 " scrolled — End to resume",
797 Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray),
798 ));
799 }
800 let hints = if app.pending().is_some() {
801 " ←/→ choose · Enter confirm · y allow · n/Esc deny"
802 } else if matches!(
803 app.status,
804 Status::Waiting | Status::Streaming | Status::Running
805 ) {
806 // Busy without a modal: the one useful key is Esc.
807 " Esc cancel · Ctrl+C quit"
808 } else {
809 " Enter send · Alt+Enter newline · Ctrl+L clear · Ctrl+C quit"
810 };
811 spans.push(Span::styled(hints, Style::default().fg(Color::DarkGray)));
812 
813 frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new(Line::from(spans)), area);
814}

fn draw_input

L815–L860

The prompt box. Its border and gutter go grey while busy, which is the visual signal that typing is frozen.

offset scrolls the prompt so the cursor's row stays visible once the text exceeds MAX_INPUT_ROWS — the prompt box scrolls internally rather than growing without bound.

The "> " marker is drawn only on the true first row (i == 0 && offset == 0), so scrolling down inside a long prompt does not leave a stray prompt character mid-text.

set_cursor_position is what makes the terminal's real cursor appear in the right cell, and it is skipped while busy — no cursor is drawn when input is frozen. The + 2 is the gutter width; this is the line where the wrap-it-ourselves decision finally pays off, since cursor_col is already an exact cell count.

815 
816fn draw_input(
817 frame: &mut Frame,
818 app: &App,
819 area: Rect,
820 layout: &crate::input::Layout,
821 visible_rows: u16,
822) {
823 let (border, gutter) = if app.is_busy() {
824 (Color::DarkGray, Color::DarkGray)
825 } else {
826 (Color::Blue, Color::Blue)
827 };
828 
829 let block = Block::bordered().border_style(Style::default().fg(border));
830 let inner = block.inner(area);
831 frame.render_widget(block, area);
832 
833 // Scroll the prompt so the cursor's row stays visible in a tall entry.
834 let (cursor_row, cursor_col) = layout.cursor;
835 let offset = cursor_row.saturating_sub(visible_rows.saturating_sub(1));
836 
837 let lines: Vec<Line> = layout
838 .rows
839 .iter()
840 .skip(offset as usize)
841 .take(visible_rows as usize)
842 .enumerate()
843 .map(|(i, row)| {
844 let marker = if i == 0 && offset == 0 { "> " } else { " " };
845 Line::from(vec![
846 Span::styled(marker, Style::default().fg(gutter)),
847 Span::raw(row.clone()),
848 ])
849 })
850 .collect();
851 
852 frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new(Text::from(lines)), inner);
853 
854 if !app.is_busy() {
855 frame.set_cursor_position(Position::new(
856 inner.x + 2 + cursor_col,
857 inner.y + cursor_row.saturating_sub(offset),
858 ));
859 }
860}

What the tests cover

913 lines, using ratatui's TestBackend — an in-memory buffer, so the tests assert on what the screen would actually say without needing a terminal.

What they pin down: the prompt box growing with input and stopping at MAX_INPUT_ROWS, each status label appearing for its state, the approval modal rendering a command, a write preview, and a -/+ diff, frames being hidden until debug is on, long content being truncated with the "… N more lines" marker, and the cursor landing on the right cell after a wrap.

Several tests render at deliberately hostile sizes — a very narrow or very short terminal — since that is where layout arithmetic tends to panic.
